note:
A 471-SECOND PAGE EXAMINED TWO STRUCTURAL TYPES OUT OF EIGHT, AND REPORTED `found: 0` FOR THE REST. Not zero links on the page -- 340 of them, and 165 graphics, named by the cross-check. The per-field activation probe spent the whole budget and five sweeps never ran.

THE ONLY THING THAT SAID SO WAS A CROSS-CHECK NOTHING READS BY DEFAULT. `structureCrossCheck` recorded `sweepEntries 0, oracleDistinctNames 340` and no gate, report or summary consults it. A capture that examined nothing and a capture that found nothing are indistinguishable everywhere downstream -- which is this project's oldest defect (an unchecked thing reported as a clean one) reaching the evidence itself rather than a check.

WHAT SCALES IS THE PER-FIELD PROBE, NOT THE PAGE. `sweepEveryStructuralType` passes `onItem: onFormField` for one sweep and nothing else; `onFormField` activates the control, presses Escape and waits for speech to settle. 100 fields at 1,478 ms per trip against 156-180 for every other type on the same page.

AND THE INSTRUMENT COULD NOT HAVE TOLD ANYONE. `trips` counts sweep navigation and NOT the activation, the Escape or the settle -- so `worker:compare`'s own rule (ms up with trips flat means each trip is slower; trips up means walking more) would have given the WRONG answer here with entirely real numbers.

THIS DOES NOT SAY `probeForms` IS WASTE: it is how 3.3.1 and 4.1.3 become reachable at all. It says where the time goes. n=1 per page; every per-type figure is a single observation. Corrected on #311's record, which names the window the wrong cause stood in (09:20Z to 11:0xZ) rather than quietly acquiring the right answer. (Measured by `orchestrator`, who ran the replay; recorded by `product-manager`.)
